handoff.summary: Adapter batch engineering-finance-adapters-b01 (curator compat-finance-adapters): two brief-11 records (data/curation/corrections/adapter-finance-brief-11.md). F1 engineering-finance--periodic-rate-for-loan-schedule carries periodic_rate/1 from the rate-year nominal-conversion context into the fixed-rate loan context (pure identity bridge). F2 engineering-finance--real-rate-as-unit-frequency-nominal carries Fisher real_rate/1 into the lump-sum nominal_rate/1 port, guarded to m==1 via paired m>=1/m<=1 guards. Both records are runtime-ready with project-derivation sources citing both bridged records; references replay the bridged records' published oracles through the identities.

assumptions: The periodic rate per compounding period is numerically identical to the effective rate per loan payment period when the loan payment period coincides with the nominal-rate compounding period; this bridge asserts that coincidence and relabels the context accordingly.

Scope: the loan-context output feeds only the end-of-period level-payment amortization-schedule family (engineering-finance--level-loan-periodic-payment@r2.runtime1 input i and, through it, the loan-payment-interest/principal-portion schedule splits); annuity-due timing, zero-rate loans, and other schedule families are outside this bridge.

assumptions: Validity only at unit compounding frequency: this identity holds only for m==1 (annual compounding), where the nominal annual rate is definitionally the rate per single annual period; at any other frequency the nominal/per-period relation needs the periodic-rate conversion first.

Price-basis discipline: the carried rate is a real rate, so the downstream lump-sum computation runs on a real (constant-dollar) basis and its P and F are real amounts, per the Fisher record's same-period same-currency context.

relationship.original_equation: r_nominal = r_real at m = 1 (annual compounding; per-period rate equals nominal rate)
relationship.translation_notes: At unit compounding frequency the nominal annual rate equals the per-period rate, so the Fisher real rate passes through unchanged as the lump-sum nominal rate (expression rreal + 0*m: identity on the rate, with m present so the guards can confine scope; the m term contributes zero at every m). Guards m>=1 and m<=1 jointly enforce m==1 because each guard is one comparison. No guard on rreal: negative real rates (inflation above nominal) pass through and the lump-sum record's r>=0 guard rejects them fail-closed at its own port.
